claims.text: Although stamp duty is generally calculated on the value of the property conveyed without deductions (as seen in Western Province Financial Statute s48), the specific rate of stamp duty for a Deed of Transfer of land in Galle (Southern Province) is not specified in the provided texts, making the calculation of the payable stamp duty on Rs. 100,000,000 impossible.

The stamp duty on the instrument must be paid prior to, or at the time of, the execution of the instrument. The mode of payment is by means of affixing adhesive stamps or impressed stamps to the required value; alternatively, if it is not practicable to use stamps, payment can be made to the Commissioner General who will endorse the payment on the instrument. The specific payment location or prescribed bank for land transfers in the Southern Province is not provided.

hits.excerpt: 48. (1) Where any property is conveyed by an instrument, the stamp duty with which such instrument is chargeable shall be calculated on the value of the property conveyed. (2) Where any property transferred for a consideration is subject to any mortgage, encumbrances or reservation of interest, stamp duty with which the instrument of transfer is chargeable shall be calculated on the value of the property transferred, without any deduction for the mortgage, encumbrances or reservation. (3) Where any property is gifted subject to any reservation in favour of the donor or any other person, stamp duty with which the instrument of gift is chargeable shall be calculated on the value of the property gifted as if that property had been gifted to the donee without that reservation.

claims.text: Upon receiving certified copies of cadastral maps, the Commissioner of Title Settlement is required to publish a Notice in the Gazette calling for claimants to the specified land parcel to submit their claims within a prescribed period.

A District Court may make an order of Declaration of Title in favor of a claimant to the whole land parcel or to a divided portion, provided that divided portion does not fall below the prescribed minimum extent.

While the law permits the Commissioner to call for claims from claimants, the retrieved sections do not contain any provisions specifying whether both an owner and occupier can make an application, or whether an application can be rejected without an inquiry.
The provided sections do not state that registration of a deed affecting land is mandatory.

An unregistered instrument executed or made on or after January 1, 1864, is void against all parties claiming an adverse interest thereto on valuable consideration by virtue of any subsequent instrument which is duly registered.
Fraud or collusion in obtaining a subsequent instrument or in securing its prior registration defeats the priority of the person claiming under it.
Registration of an instrument does not cure any defect in the instrument or confer upon it any effect or validity other than the priority conferred by section 7.

The Registration of Documents Ordinance acknowledges that registration is initiated by 'the person who presented it for registration or his agent', without further defining who is authorized to do so for ordinary deeds.
A caveator who has or claims to have a right, title, or interest to a land, undivided land, land parcel, or condominium parcel may present a caveat for registration.

claims.text: Under the provided provisions, specific persons authorized to present documents include: a judgment creditor who may present a seizure priority notice (SRC005:s31(1)), and a caveator (a person who has or claims to have a right, title, or interest to a land, undivided land, land parcel, or condominium parcel) who may present a caveat (SRC009:s32(1)(a)). The ordinance also refers generally to an authorized person or their agent presenting an instrument, though the general definition of authorized presenters is not fully detailed in the provided sections.

Under the Ordinance, a Registrar may refuse to register an instrument if they suspect the presenter is not authorized until the right to present is proved, or if the instrument does not comply with the Ordinance or any written law affecting its form or mode of execution. Additionally, a Registrar is mandated to refuse registration if the instrument is liable to stamp duty but is not duly stamped, or until any registration fee is paid.

If an error or omission is shown to the satisfaction of the Registrar-General, they must issue a written notice in the prescribed form: (a) to the parties for a deed, (b) to the executor or administrator for a will, or (c) to the presenter for other instruments, and order the correction. The correction is made by the relevant Registrar in the prescribed manner without affecting prior accrued priority. Notice may be dispensed with if death, legal incapacity, or other sufficient cause prevents issuance. If the error and correction are in different folios, they must be cross-referenced. A person aggrieved by a refusal to make a correction order may sue in the District Court within 30 days of the communication of the refusal.

claims.text: Under the Apartment Ownership (Special Provisions) Act, No. 23 of 2018, owners of certain registered condominium properties must submit a written declaration from the Director-General of the Department of Buildings certifying the safety of occupation of the property.

The provisions mention a 'Condominium Plan' and a 'Plan of redivision or amalgamation', which can be registered or amended, but do not provide further definitions of distinct types of plans or the differences between them.

Section 24 contains a heading stating 'Provisions of Partition Act not to apply in certain cases', but the substantive text explaining the details of this restriction is not contained in the provided text.

claims.text: Under the Stamp Duty Act 1982 and the Western Province Financial Statute 1990, when property is gifted subject to a reservation in favour of the donor or another person, the stamp duty is calculated on the value of the property as if it had been gifted without that reservation. However, there is no information regarding the specific valuation positions before and after 31 March 1977.

The stamp duty on the Deed of Gift from Mark Perera to Peter Perera must be calculated on the value of the property gifted as if it had been gifted without the reservation of the life interest, but the exact stamp duty payable cannot be computed because the stamp duty rate schedule is missing.

hits.excerpt: 48. (1) Where any property is conveyed by an instrument, the stamp duty with which such instrument is chargeable shall be calculated on the value of the property conveyed. (2) Where any property transferred for a consideration is subject to any mortgage, encumbrances or reservation of interest, stamp duty with which the instrument of transfer is chargeable shall be calculated on the value of the property transferred, without any deduction for the mortgage, encumbrances or reservation. (3) Where any property is gifted subject to any reservation in favour of the donor or any other person, stamp duty with which the instrument of gift is chargeable shall be calculated on the value of the property gifted as if that property had been gifted to the donee without that reservation.

claims.text: Under Section 24(c) of the Stamp Duty Act, 1982, the stamp duty on a lease or agreement to lease is payable by the lessee or intended lessee (Sheela), unless there is an agreement to the contrary. However, the precise calculation of the stamp duty cannot be performed because the applicable rate schedule is missing from the provided statutes.

Under Section 2 of the Powers of Attorney Ordinance, a power of attorney is a written authority given by one person to another to perform any work or do any act. Since Visaka's 2017 Special Power of Attorney is restricted to selling the Colombo house, she does not have the authority to execute a lease agreement, and Mala must grant a new power of attorney specifically for leasing.

If Mala executes the new power of attorney in Sri Lanka, Section 3A of the Powers of Attorney (Amendment) Act, No. 28 of 2022 requires that it be duly attested by a notary public and contain a description of the land with its metes, bounds, and extent.

If Mala executes the power of attorney while abroad, Section 2 of the Powers of Attorney Ordinance (as amended by Section 2 of the Powers of Attorney (Amendment) Act, No. 3 of 2024) allows a power of attorney to be executed before or attested by an Ambassador, High Commissioner, or other diplomatic representative of Sri Lanka.

claims.text: Under the Apartment Ownership Law, a Condominium Plan must contain a declaration in the prescribed form made by the applicant and attested by a Notary Public. This declaration must include: a reference-based description of the land's boundaries, extent, and situation; the name and address of the property owners; particulars of title deeds, instruments, and registration details under the Registration of Documents Ordinance; particulars of any known encumbrances or lis pendens; a description of the building's storeys, basements, and units; unit details such as floor area, room count, and accessory units; a description of the common elements and the percentage of undivided share appurtenant to each unit; restrictions on use; and the signatures of the owners.
